cards.q: Solve the equation −x² + 6x − 4 = 0. Give each solution correct to one decimal place.
cards.hook: Brackets round every negative: 2a = 2(−1) = −2, not 2.

cards.q: You solve −x² + 6x − 4 = 0 with the quadratic formula. What is b² − 4ac, the number under the square root?
cards.hook: Bracket every negative: −4(−1)(−4) = −16.

cards.q: Find the co-ordinates of the turning point of the function f(x) = −x² + 6x − 4.
cards.why: f′(x) = −2x + 6 = 0 gives x = 3. Then f(3) = −9 + 18 − 4 = 5, so the turning point is (3, 5).
cards.hook: Slope 0 finds the x; the original f(x) finds the y. −3² is −9.

cards.q: To find the turning point of f(x) = −x² + 6x − 4, which equation do you solve first?
cards.why: At a turning point the curve is flat, so its slope f′(x) is 0. f′(x) = −2x + 6 (the −4 goes), so solve −2x + 6 = 0. f(x) = 0 gives the roots instead.
cards.hook: Turning point: slope = 0, so f′(x) = 0, not f(x) = 0.

cards.q: Sketch y = −x² + 6x − 4 using its roots x ≈ 0.8 and x ≈ 5.2 and its turning point (3, 5). What must the sketch show to get full marks?
cards.right: Roots, top at (3, 5), scale on both axes
wrong: Roots and top at (3, 5); no scale
Ruled lines joining the three points
A U shape with its bottom at (3, 5)
cards.why: One smooth upside-down U (the −x² flips it) through (0.8, 0) and (5.2, 0) with its top at (3, 5), and both axes numbered: the scale earns marks too.
cards.hook: Minus x² = a frown ∩. Number both axes before you draw.

cards.q: An oil trader's daily profit is p = 96x − 0.03x² euro, where x is the number of barrels traded. Complete the table: what is the profit when x = 1000?
cards.hook: Square first, then multiply by 0.03.

wrong: Ruled straight lines, point to point
Plot the five points; don't join them
cards.why: The x² makes the graph a curve: join all five points freehand with one smooth curve. It is still rising at 1500 and turns before 2000.
cards.hook: x² in the formula → one smooth curve, never ruled lines.

cards.q: Graph of the profit p = 96x − 0.03x²: barrels x across, profit p up. How do you use it to estimate the daily profit when 1750 barrels are traded?
cards.right: Up from 1750 barrels to the curve, across
wrong: Across from 1750 on the p axis, then down
Read the slope of the curve at x = 1750
cards.why: Profit is on the up axis. Find 1750 on the barrels axis, go up to the curve, then across to read the profit: about €76 000 (the formula gives €76 125).
cards.hook: Start on the axis you know, finish on the axis you want.
keys: go up to the curve, then across

cards.q: Graph of the profit p = 96x − 0.03x² (barrels across, profit up). A line across at €60 000 is drawn. About how many barrels are traded when the daily profit is €60 000?
cards.why: The line across at €60 000 cuts the hill-shaped curve twice, once going up and once coming down: about 850 and about 2350 barrels. Give both.
cards.hook: A line across a hill can cut it twice: give both answers.

cards.q: Daily profit p = 96x − 0.03x² for x barrels. Use calculus to find the number of barrels traded that will earn the maximum daily profit.
cards.why: dp/dx = 96 − 0.06x (2 × 0.03 = 0.06). At the maximum the slope is 0: 96 − 0.06x = 0, so x = 96 ÷ 0.06 = 1600 barrels.
cards.hook: Max or min: set the derivative equal to 0.

cards.q: The daily profit is p = 96x − 0.03x². What is dp/dx?
cards.why: 96x becomes 96. For 0.03x², bring the 2 down (2 × 0.03 = 0.06) and take one off the power: 0.06x. So dp/dx = 96 − 0.06x.
cards.hook: Power down in front, then one off the power.

cards.q: The profit p = 96x − 0.03x² is greatest when x = 1600 barrels (dp/dx = 96 − 0.06x). Find this maximum daily profit.
cards.why: Put x = 1600 into the profit function itself, not into dp/dx: p = 96(1600) − 0.03(1600)² = 153 600 − 76 800 = €76 800.
cards.hook: Derivative says WHERE the max is; the function says HOW BIG it is.

cards.q: Daily profit p = 96x − 0.03x² for x barrels. The trader will not make a profit if he trades more than k barrels of oil in a day. Calculate k.
cards.why: No profit means p = 0: 96x − 0.03x² = 0, so x(96 − 0.03x) = 0. x = 0 is trading nothing; the other gives x = 96 ÷ 0.03 = 3200.
cards.hook: Break-even: set the profit itself to 0, not its derivative.

cards.q: f(x) = x³ + x² − 2x + 7. Find the co-ordinates of the point where the graph of f cuts the y-axis.
cards.why: Every point on the y-axis has x = 0: f(0) = 0 + 0 − 2(0) + 7 = 7, so the graph cuts the y-axis at (0, 7).
cards.hook: y-axis: put x = 0. x-axis: put y = 0.

cards.q: f(x) = x³ + x² − 2x + 7. How do you verify, using algebra, that the point A(1, 7) is on the graph of f?
cards.why: A point is on the graph when its x, put into f, gives its y: f(1) = 1 + 1 − 2 + 7 = 7, the same as the y of A(1, 7).
cards.hook: On the graph means: put in x, get out y.

cards.q: f(x) = x³ + x² − 2x + 7. Find f′(x), the derivative of f(x).
cards.why: Bring each power down and take one off: x³ → 3x², x² → 2x, −2x → −2, and the 7 on its own → 0. So f′(x) = 3x² + 2x − 2.
cards.hook: Power down in front, one off the power; a number on its own vanishes.

cards.q: f(x) = x³ + x² − 2x + 7 and f′(x) = 3x² + 2x − 2. What is the slope of the tangent to the graph of f when x = 1?
cards.why: The slope of the tangent is f′(1), not f(1): f′(1) = 3(1)² + 2(1) − 2 = 3 + 2 − 2 = 3.
cards.hook: Slope → put x into f′(x). Height → put x into f(x).

cards.q: The tangent to the graph of f(x) = x³ + x² − 2x + 7 at the point A(1, 7) has slope 3. Find the equation of the tangent.
cards.why: Use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) with (1, 7) and m = 3: y − 7 = 3(x − 1), so y − 7 = 3x − 3 and y = 3x + 4.
cards.hook: A line needs a point and a slope: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).

cards.q: Kieran has 21 m of fencing to enclose a rectangular garden of length x m and width y m. Which equation for the perimeter leads to y = 10.5 − x?
cards.why: The perimeter is two lengths and two widths, all 21 m of fencing: 2x + 2y = 21. Divide by 2: x + y = 10.5, so y = 10.5 − x.
cards.hook: Perimeter = all the way round: 2 lengths + 2 widths.

cards.q: Kieran's garden has length x m and width y = 10.5 − x m. Complete the table: what are y and the area A when x = 7?
cards.why: y = 10.5 − 7 = 3.5 m. The area of a rectangle is length × width, so A = 7 × 3.5 = 24.5 m².
cards.hook: Area multiplies length × width; perimeter adds all four sides.

cards.q: One column of Kieran's table reads x = 3 m, y = 7.5 m, A = 22.5 m². You plot the graph of A (up) against x (across). Which point do you plot for this column?
cards.why: Points are (across, up). The graph is A against x: x = 3 across, A = 22.5 up, so plot (3, 22.5). The width y is not plotted.
cards.hook: (x, y) means across first, then up.

cards.q: On your graph of the garden's area A (up) against its length x (across), how do you estimate the maximum area and the length that gives it?
cards.right: Top of the curve: across to A, down to x
wrong: Top of the curve: down to A, across to x
Where the curve meets the x-axis
The right-hand end of the curve, x = 10
cards.why: The maximum area is the highest point of the curve. Read across to the A axis (about 27.5 m²) and down to the x axis (about 5.25 m).
cards.hook: Max = the top of the hill. Across for its height, down for its x.

cards.q: Kieran's rectangular garden has length x m and width y = 10.5 − x m. Write its area A in terms of x only.
cards.why: Area = length × width = x × y. Replace y with 10.5 − x and multiply out: A = x(10.5 − x) = 10.5x − x².
cards.hook: Max/min problems: first get the thing you want in ONE letter.

cards.q: The area of Kieran's garden is A = 10.5x − x². Find dA/dx.
cards.why: 10.5x differentiates to 10.5 (the x goes, the number stays). For x², bring the 2 down and take one off: 2x. So dA/dx = 10.5 − 2x.
cards.hook: ax → a; x² → 2x; a number on its own → 0.

cards.q: The garden's area is A = 10.5x − x² and dA/dx = 10.5 − 2x. Find the value of x which will give the maximum area.
cards.why: At the maximum the slope is 0: 10.5 − 2x = 0, so 2x = 10.5 and x = 10.5 ÷ 2 = 5.25 m.
cards.hook: Biggest area → slope 0 → solve dA/dx = 0.

cards.q: The area of Kieran's garden is A = 10.5x − x². Why is dA/dx = 0 at the length that gives the maximum area?
cards.right: The curve is flat at its top: slope 0
wrong: The area is 0 at the top
The length x is 0 at the top
dA/dx is at its largest at the top
cards.why: dA/dx is the slope of the area graph. Going up to the top the slope is positive, after it negative: at the top it is 0, so the curve is flat there.
cards.hook: Top of a hill: flat for a moment, so the slope is 0.

cards.q: Kieran's garden: area A = 10.5x − x², dA/dx = 10.5 − 2x, and the maximum is at length x = 5.25 m. Find this maximum area.
cards.why: Put x = 5.25 into A, not into dA/dx. The width is 10.5 − 5.25 = 5.25 m too, so A = 5.25 × 5.25 = 27.5625 ≈ 27.56 m².
cards.hook: The derivative finds where; the area formula finds how much.

cards.q: Find the two values of x for which 3x² − 6x − 8 = 0. Give each answer correct to 1 decimal place.
cards.hook: −b of a negative b is positive; (−6)² = +36; 2a = 6.

cards.q: You use the quadratic formula to solve 3x² − 6x − 8 = 0. What are a, b and c?
cards.why: Match 3x² − 6x − 8 = 0 to ax² + bx + c = 0 and keep each sign with its number: a = 3, b = −6, c = −8.
cards.hook: The sign in front belongs to the number: −6x gives b = −6.
keys: keep each sign with its number

cards.q: Find the co-ordinates of the minimum point of the function f(x) = 3x² − 6x − 8.
cards.why: f′(x) = 6x − 6. At the minimum 6x − 6 = 0, so x = 1. Then y = f(1) = 3 − 6 − 8 = −11: the minimum point is (1, −11).
cards.hook: Co-ordinates = x AND y. The y comes from f(x), not f′(x).

cards.q: f(x) = 3x² − 6x − 8. Solving f′(x) = 6x − 6 = 0 gives x = 1 at the minimum point. How do you get its y co-ordinate?
wrong: No need: x = 1 is the answer
cards.why: The point is on the curve, so its height comes from f itself: f(1) = 3(1)² − 6(1) − 8 = −11. f′(1) = 0 is only the slope there.
cards.hook: f′(x) = 0 finds the x; f(x) finds the y. Give both.

cards.q: A company's weekly profit is P(x) = 275x − x² − 2000 euro, where x is the km of cable sold. How much money does it lose if it sells no cable?
cards.why: Selling no cable means x = 0, and 275 × 0 = 0: P(0) = 0 − 0 − 2000 = −2000. A profit of −€2000 is a loss of €2000.
cards.hook: Nothing sold → put x = 0. A negative profit is a loss.

cards.q: Profit P(x) = 275x − x² − 2000 euro for x km of cable, and at most 200 km can be sold. One week the profit was €8350. How many km were sold?
cards.why: 275x − x² − 2000 = 8350 gives x² − 275x + 10 350 = 0, so (x − 45)(x − 230) = 0. At most 200 km can be sold, so x = 45 km.
cards.hook: Check every answer against the limits: here x ≤ 200.

cards.q: Profit P(x) = 275x − x² − 2000 euro for x km of cable. Which equation finds the km sold in a week when the profit was €8350?
cards.why: The profit itself is €8350, so set P(x) = 8350 and keep the −2000. The derivative 275 − 2x is the rate the profit changes, not the profit.
cards.hook: Amount given → set P(x) to it. Rate given → set P′(x) to it.

cards.q: Profit P(x) = 275x − x² − 2000 euro for x km of cable. Complete the table: what is the profit when x = 50?
cards.hook: Square first, keep every minus, and don't drop the −2000.

cards.right: Smooth curve, rising more and more slowly
wrong: Smooth curve, rising faster and faster
One straight line through the points
Ruled lines from point to point
cards.why: The profit goes up by 1650, 1450, 1250, 1050, 850: still rising, but by less each time. Join the points with one smooth curve that bends over.
cards.hook: Look at the gaps: shrinking gaps = a curve that flattens.

cards.q: Graph of the profit P (up, in €) against km of cable sold x (across). How do you find the sales that give a profit between €10 000 and €14 000?
wrong: Up from 10 000 and 14 000 on the km axis
Put x = 10 000 and x = 14 000 into P(x)
cards.why: Profit is on the up axis. Draw lines across at €10 000 and €14 000 to the curve, then down: about 55 km and 83 km. Sales between them work.
cards.hook: Know the profit? Start on the profit axis, go across, then down.

cards.q: Profit P(x) = 275x − x² − 2000 euro for x km of cable. Use calculus to find the km sold when the profit is increasing at a rate of €105 per km.
cards.why: The rate the profit increases is P′(x) = 275 − 2x. Set it equal to 105: 275 − 2x = 105, so 2x = 170 and x = 85 km.
cards.hook: Rate of change = derivative. Set P′(x) equal to the rate given.

cards.q: Profit P(x) = 275x − x² − 2000. The profit is increasing at a rate of €105 per km. Which equation do you solve?
cards.why: "Increasing at a rate of" means the derivative: P′(x) = 275 − 2x (the −2000 goes to 0). Set it equal to 105, not to 0.
cards.hook: Rate → P′(x). Amount → P(x). Max or min → P′(x) = 0.

cards.q: A quadratic graph cuts the y-axis at height 6 (point A) and the x-axis at −2 (point B) and at 3 (point C). Write down the co-ordinates of A, B and C.
cards.why: On the y-axis x = 0, so A = (0, 6). On the x-axis y = 0, so B = (−2, 0) and C = (3, 0). Co-ordinates are (across, up).
cards.hook: (x, y): across first, then up. On the x-axis, y = 0.

cards.q: A quadratic graph is an upside-down U that cuts the x-axis at x = −2 and x = 3, and the y-axis at 6. Which formula fits it?
cards.why: Each root gives a factor with its sign changed: x = −2 → (x + 2), x = 3 → (x − 3). The ∩ needs a minus in front: −(x + 2)(x − 3) = −x² + x + 6.
cards.hook: Root −2 → factor (x + 2): change the sign.

cards.q: The quadratic with roots −2 and 3 and an upside-down U shape is f(x) = −(x + 2)(x − 3). Multiply it out.
cards.why: (x + 2)(x − 3) = x² − 3x + 2x − 6 = x² − x − 6. The minus in front changes every sign: −x² + x + 6.
cards.hook: Multiply out the brackets first, then flip every sign.

cards.q: f(x) = −x² + x + 6. Use calculus to find the maximum point of f(x).
cards.why: f′(x) = −2x + 1 = 0 gives x = 0.5. Then f(0.5) = −0.25 + 0.5 + 6 = 6.25, so the maximum point is (0.5, 6.25).
cards.hook: −(0.5)² = −0.25: square first, then put the minus in front.

cards.q: f(x) = −x² + x + 6. What is f′(x)?
cards.why: −x² → −2x (bring the 2 down and keep the minus), x → 1, and the 6 on its own → 0. So f′(x) = −2x + 1.
cards.hook: Keep the sign in front when you bring the power down.

cards.q: The amount of a drug in the bloodstream t hours after it is taken is C(t) = −t³ + 4.5t² + 54t units. What is the amount after 4 hours?
cards.hook: Powers first: 4³ = 64 and 4² = 16, then multiply.

cards.q: Drug amount C(t) = −t³ + 4.5t² + 54t units after t hours. Complete the table: what is C(3)?
cards.hook: Bracket the number: −(3)³ = −27, and 3² = 9 before × 4.5.

cards.q: Graph of the drug amount C(t): time t in hours across, amount in units up. How do you use it to estimate the amount after 3½ hours?
cards.right: Up from 3.5 on the time axis, then across
wrong: Up from 3.3 on the time axis, then across
Across from 3.5 on the amount axis, down
Read the slope of the curve at t = 3.5
cards.why: 3½ hours is 3.5 (not 3.3: half an hour is 0.5). Go up from 3.5 on the time axis to the curve, then across: about 200 units.
cards.hook: Time is across: start there. 3½ h = 3.5, not 3.3.

cards.q: Graph of the drug amount C(t) against time t (hours). Going across from 100 units to the curve and down, you reach 1.75 on the time axis. How long after taking the drug is that?
cards.why: 1.75 hours is 1 hour and 0.75 of an hour: 0.75 × 60 = 45 minutes. So about 1 hour 45 minutes.
cards.hook: Decimal hours → minutes: multiply the decimal part by 60.

cards.q: Drug amount C(t) = −t³ + 4.5t² + 54t. Find, in terms of t, the rate at which the drug amount is changing after t hours.
cards.why: Rate of change = derivative. Bring each power down and take one off: −t³ → −3t², 4.5t² → 9t (2 × 4.5), 54t → 54.
cards.hook: "Rate at which it is changing" = differentiate.

cards.q: Drug amount C(t) = −t³ + 4.5t² + 54t units after t hours. "The rate at which the drug amount is changing after t hours" means which of these?
wrong: C(t) ÷ t, the amount per hour
cards.why: A rate of change is the derivative: how fast C is going up or down at that moment. C(t) is the amount, and C(t) ÷ t is only an average.
cards.hook: "Rate", "how fast", "increasing at" → the derivative.
keys: A rate of change is the derivative

cards.q: The drug amount changes at the rate C′(t) = −3t² + 9t + 54 units per hour. Find the rate at which the drug amount is changing after 4 hours.
cards.why: Put t = 4 into the derivative, not into C(t): C′(4) = −3(16) + 9(4) + 54 = −48 + 36 + 54 = 42 units per hour.
cards.hook: Rate → C′(t). Amount → C(t).

cards.q: C(t) = −t³ + 4.5t² + 54t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 9, and C′(t) = −3t² + 9t + 54. Find the maximum amount of the drug in the bloodstream over the first 9 hours.
cards.why: Set C′(t) = 0 and divide by −3: t² − 3t − 18 = 0, so (t − 6)(t + 3) = 0 and t = 6 (not −3). C(6) = −216 + 162 + 324 = 270 units.
cards.hook: C′(t) = 0 finds WHEN; C(t) finds HOW MUCH.

cards.q: At the maximum drug amount C′(t) = −3t² + 9t + 54 = 0. Dividing by −3 gives t² − 3t − 18 = 0. Which time do you use?
cards.why: (t − 6)(t + 3) = 0 gives t = 6 or t = −3. The time after taking the drug can't be negative, so t = 6 hours.
cards.hook: Check roots against the story: time can't be negative.

cards.q: The drug amount changes at the rate C′(t) = −3t² + 9t + 54 units per hour. Which shows the amount is decreasing 7 hours after the drug was taken?
cards.why: C′(7) = −3(49) + 9(7) + 54 = −147 + 63 + 54 = −30. A negative rate means the amount is going down, by 30 units per hour.
cards.hook: Sign of the derivative: + going up, − going down.

cards.q: f(x) = −x³ + 4x² + x − 2. Complete the table: what is f(−1)?
cards.hook: Bracket the negative: (−1)³ = −1, so −(−1)³ = +1.

cards.q: You have drawn the graph of f(x) = −x³ + 4x² + x − 2 for −1 ≤ x ≤ 4. Where on the graph do you read the two roots of f(x)?
cards.right: Where the curve cuts the x-axis
wrong: Where the curve cuts the y-axis
At the bottom and top of the curve
At the two ends, x = −1 and x = 4
cards.why: A root is where f(x) = 0, a height of 0: where the curve cuts the x-axis. It crosses twice in this domain, at about x = −0.7 and x = 0.7.
cards.hook: Roots = where the curve cuts the x-axis (height 0).

cards.q: f(x) = −x³ + 4x² + x − 2. Find the value of x for which f″(x) = 0, where f″(x) is the second derivative of f(x).
cards.why: f′(x) = −3x² + 8x + 1. Differentiate again: f″(x) = −6x + 8. Then −6x + 8 = 0 gives 6x = 8, so x = 8/6 = 4/3.
cards.hook: f″: differentiate, then differentiate again.

cards.q: f(x) = −x³ + 4x² + x − 2. What is f″(x), the second derivative?
cards.why: First f′(x) = −3x² + 8x + 1 (the −2 goes). Differentiate again: −3x² → −6x, 8x → 8, 1 → 0. So f″(x) = −6x + 8.
cards.hook: Second derivative = differentiate twice. Numbers on their own vanish.

cards.q: A ball is hit straight up. Its height is f(t) = −4t² + 16t + 1 metres, t seconds after it is hit. At what height was the ball when it was hit?
cards.why: When the ball is hit, no time has passed: t = 0. f(0) = −4(0)² + 16(0) + 1 = 1 m.
cards.hook: At the start, t = 0.

cards.q: Ball height f(t) = −4t² + 16t + 1 metres after t seconds. Complete the table: what is the height at t = 0.5?
cards.hook: Square first: 0.5² = 0.25, not 1. Then × −4.

cards.q: Ball height f(t) = −4t² + 16t + 1 m. Your table stops at t = 4 s, when the ball is still 1 m up. How do you use the graph to find how long it was in the air?
cards.right: Extend the curve to the time axis, read t
wrong: Read the last time in the table, t = 4
Read the time at the top of the curve
Read where the curve meets the height axis
cards.why: The ball is in the air until its height is 0, so carry the curve down to the time axis: it lands just after t = 4, at about 4.1 s.
cards.hook: Landed = height 0 = on the time axis.

cards.q: Ball height f(t) = −4t² + 16t + 1 m. A line across at 10 m cuts the graph at about t = 0.6 s and t = 3.4 s. For how long was the ball 10 m or more above the ground?
cards.why: The ball passes 10 m going up (t ≈ 0.6 s) and coming down (t ≈ 3.4 s). Length of time = later − earlier = 3.4 − 0.6 = 2.8 s.
cards.hook: "How long" = later time minus earlier time.

cards.q: Ball height f(t) = −4t² + 16t + 1. Find f′(t), the derivative of f(t).
cards.why: −4t² → 2 × (−4)t = −8t, 16t → 16, and the 1 on its own → 0. So f′(t) = −8t + 16.
cards.hook: Bring the power down and multiply: 2 × (−4) = −8.

cards.q: Ball height f(t) = −4t² + 16t + 1 m, and f′(t) = −8t + 16. Find the speed of the ball when it had been in the air for 4 seconds.
cards.why: Speed comes from the derivative: f′(4) = −8(4) + 16 = −32 + 16 = −16. The minus only says the ball is falling, so the speed is 16 m/s.
cards.hook: Height → f(t). Speed → f′(t).

cards.q: For the ball, f′(4) = −16, where f′(t) is the rate its height changes in m/s. What does the minus sign tell you?
wrong: The ball is 16 m below the pitch
The ball is going up at 16 m/s
cards.why: f′(t) is the rate the height changes. Negative means the height is going down: the ball is falling at 16 m/s. It says nothing about where the ball is.
cards.hook: Sign of the derivative: + rising, − falling.
keys: the ball is falling at 16 m/s

cards.q: Ball height f(t) = −4t² + 16t + 1 m, and f′(t) = −8t + 16. Find the time t when the ball was descending at a speed of 8 m/s.
cards.why: Descending means the height is falling, so the rate is negative: f′(t) = −8. −8t + 16 = −8 gives 8t = 24, so t = 3 s. (+8 gives t = 1, still rising.)
cards.hook: Going down → negative derivative.
